summary: Internal planning to re-evaluate Q3 roadmap priorities after a launch incident caused a latency spike tied to a new quantization kernel. Team agreed to postpone broad rollout, run targeted perf fixes, and strengthen canary/telemetry gating.
meeting_header: Date: 2026-06-30 | Start: 14:00 UTC | Duration: 75m | Attendees: Maya Patel, Jonas Rivera, Priya Singh, Leo Zhang, Sofia Morales
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Ok everyone, thanks for joining, gonna kick off, this is the Q3 roadmap + launch readiness and postmortem, uh we have about an hour and 15. Quick note: recording on.
[00:15] Jonas: hi all, Jonas here. I'll start with a quick recap of the incident, then we can talk roadmap impacts.
[00:28] Maya: yeah please, the TL;DR we saw a token-level latency spike during the canary on Friday after merging the quantization-optimized kernels.
[00:40] Jonas: right so, here's what happened, we shipped the MPI-style kernel changes for 4-bit path, on our internal dedicated nodes, during higher throughput the KV cache had much more churn than expected, and that increased the per-token latency by, uh, roughly 3x for some requests. We think it's due to the cache eviction heuristics interacting with the new memory layout.
[01:05] Priya: and to add, our tracing showed queueing at the worker level, not network, so it's compute-side. There were also some out-of-order buffer refs that look suspicious but could be an artifact of the profiler.
[01:22] Leo: QA reproduced on staging with long-context prompts and large batch sizes, notably when sequence length > 1024 and batch sizes over 8 combo. So it's not universal but a clear regression edge case.
[01:38] Maya: ok that's helpful. So immediate question for roadmap: do we roll back the kernel changes for the imminent launch, or gate them behind a more aggressive canary?
[01:50] Jonas: my recommendation is to gate. Rollback is disruptive given other perf improvements depend on the change, but we should block rollout to prod and run a canary that stresses long-context, high-batch scenarios. If the canary passes with the fix, proceed; otherwise roll back.
[02:07] Priya: agree, and we'll need to update the SRE gating checklist to include token-level p95 p99 checks and a new trace for KV cache eviction rates. Currently the checklist focuses on error rates and infra metrics, not cache behavior.
[02:23] Sofia: can we add an explicit task to augment the launch checklist? I can do that and circulate.
[02:29] Maya: yes please. Sofia will own checklist update.
[02:33] Speaker 5: (mumble) also, did we talk about how this affects Dedicated customers? We had an enterprise customer testing dedicated pools.
[02:42] Jonas: good point. For Dedicated we need a mitigation path that doesn't require immediate rollback, maybe backoff to a compatible quantized variant or reduce batch sizes. But we should contact the SE/customer team and offer a manual hold.
[02:58] Maya: action: reach out to customer success for dedicated pilots, let them know we are gating. Sofia can draft the note.
[03:06] Leo: on QA side, I'll add regression tests that simulate stress: sequence, batch combos, and repeated KV cache warm/cold cycles. Found a flaky case where the cache didn't reuse prefixes as expected.
[03:23] Jonas: quick nerd-dive  the new memory layout was intended to reduce copy overhead, but it seems to increase cost when cache evictions happen frequently; the kernel includes a fast path that assumes stable cache. With noise we hit the slow path more often. Looking into heuristics to prefer stable entries, or to prefetch the KV layout differently.
[03:44] Priya: can you write up a short design doc for the heuristics and perf test plan? We need it for the execs.
[03:50] Jonas: will do, aim for 2 pages + perf spreadsheet.
[03:53] [05:12] Maya: switching to roadmap: given this incident, what should we deprioritize to keep launch date? We promised improved quantization coverage, but if it's risky maybe push it to a follow-up.
[05:26] Jonas: I'd say push the broad 4-bit rollout and focus on stability fixes for the release. Keep smaller UX features that don't affect serving runtime.
[05:36] Sofia: stakeholders care about cost reductions from quantization, but they'd rather have stable performance. Recommend we re-scope the Q3 milestone: make the perf-stability tasks mandatory and quantization expansion optional.
[05:50] Maya: ok that's a near-consensus. I'll update the roadmap doc after this call. Link: https://internal.redwood.ai/docs/q3-roadmap (note: placeholder).
[06:03] Priya: also, long-term, we should improve telemetry to automatically flag token-level latency regressions and tie them to commit hashes. Right now traces are too coarse.
[06:15] Jonas: yep, adding commit-level tagging to traces would help. I'll coordinate with instrumentation.
[06:22] Leo: QA will need environment parity updates for the canary  ensure staging mirrors production batch shapes and node counts. Found the staging nodes were smaller, so we missed the issue earlier.
[06:36] Maya: good catch. Priya, can SRE make a staging template that's production-like?
[06:40] Priya: yes, but it costs more. We'll need approval to spin dedicated staging clusters for the canary windows.
[06:47] Maya: note for finance, will raise with Ops.
[07:00] [10:05] Sofia: question: any legal/compliance concerns with delaying the launch? Some partners are on timeline.
[10:12] Maya: we should surface to GTM. But quality-first stance is defensible; we'll prepare comms.
[10:20] Jonas: technical details  potential short-term mitigations: reduce max batch size to 8 in released config, revert only the memory-layout change while keeping other micro-optimizations, and add early eviction detection. Each has tradeoffs.
[10:34] Priya: we should test each mitigation in synthetic workloads then run a canary. Also, add an abort threshold: if p99 increases by > 40% compared to baseline, abort rollout.
[10:47] Maya: ok, add abort thresholds to checklist. Sofia will add that.
[10:54] Leo: I'll draft regression suite and share link to test matrix: https://internal.redwood.ai/tests/kv-cache-regression (placeholder).
[11:05] Jonas: question about telemetry retention  current traces only kept 7 days, need 30 for post-release analysis. Ops cost impact though.
[11:15] Priya: propose 30-day retention for token-level traces but sampled; keep full traces for incidents.
[11:22] Maya: agreed. Action: Priya to propose retention plan and cost estimate.
[11:30] [25:00] Maya: open floor  anything else?
[25:10] Jonas: one more: the kernel change was based on a perf win on short sequences, so we need better per-profile testing in CI. I'll add per-sequence-length benchmarks in the CI perf suite.
[25:24] Sofia: and I'm adding stakeholders to the roadmap doc; we'll ask execs for a final call next week.
[25:32] Maya: recap: gate rollout, run targeted perf fixes, update checklist and telemetry, run canary with production-like staging, communicate to customers and execs, and schedule follow-up.
[25:46] Priya: agree.
[25:50] Maya: next meeting  quick sync in 1 week, same time, to review perf results and canary plan. I'll send invite.
[25:58] Jonas: noted.
[26:02] Leo: noted.
[26:05] Maya: ok thanks everyone. End call.
[26:12] (end)
